item.title: CISA reaches October 4 compliance deadline for actively exploited Fortinet FortiMail path traversal zero day CVE-2026-104286
item.description:
Federal civilian executive branch agencies face today's mandatory compliance deadline under Binding Operational Directive 26-04 to remediate an actively exploited email security gateway vulnerability. Unpatched systems face mandatory disconnection orders across federal enterprise networks.
The mandatory remediation mandate applies to Fortinet FortiMail path traversal vulnerability CVE-2026-104286 with a CVSS score of 9.8. Threat actors exploit improper URI path normalization and NULL character handling within web management handlers to bypass path restrictions, writing arbitrary files to the host operating system and executing system commands. CISA ordered federal agencies to apply vendor updates or enforce temporary CLI workarounds disabling Identity-Based Encryption IBE features.
Subverting secure email gateways exposes corporate messaging streams and identity verification pathways. Because FortiMail appliances process incoming enterprise email traffic and manage user directory connections, an unauthenticated gateway takeover permits threat actors to intercept sensitive communications, harvest employee credentials, and pivot into internal subnets.
- Force immediate installation of official security updates published by Fortinet across all FortiMail appliance deployments. - Apply temporary workarounds disabling Identity-Based Encryption IBE features via command-line interface where patches cannot be immediately installed. - Restrict public internet access to FortiMail web management portals using dedicated out-of-band management subnets. - Inspect system access logs for malformed URI paths containing NULL characters or unverified file modification requests.
Perimeter email gateway protection demands strict adherence to threat-informed remediation deadlines and proactive access control microsegmentation to ensure messaging controllers remain protected from unauthenticated path traversal exploits. #CodeDefence #Fortinet #FortiMail #CISA #KEV #PathTraversal #RCE #EmailSecurity #AppSec

item.title: CISA fast tracks Zammad session fixation CVE-2026-102489 and privilege management flaw CVE-2026-102490 to KEV catalog
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity regulators have expanded the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to order priority remediation for two web application flaws in open-source customer support software. Threat actors actively exploit session fixation and privilege manipulation logic to hijack active support agent sessions.
The catalog additions cover Zammad session fixation vulnerability CVE-2026-102489 and improper privilege management vulnerability CVE-2026-102490 under Binding Operational Directive 26-04. Confirmed threat telemetry indicates adversaries issuing crafted HTTP request sequences to fixate user session tokens, allowing unauthenticated attackers to hijack authenticated helpdesk agent sessions and modify role-based access control RBAC parameters across enterprise customer service portals.
Subverting helpdesk and customer support platforms introduces severe data exposure and privilege escalation risks. Because ticketing systems store sensitive customer communications, internal system credentials, and personal data, an unauthenticated session hijack enables threat actors to harvest customer records and manipulate internal access permissions.
- Upgrade Zammad open-source helpdesk installations immediately to current patched maintenance release builds. - Invalidate active user session tokens and enforce mandatory re-authentication across all helpdesk support accounts. - Inspect web application access logs for anomalous session identifier tokens or unverified role adjustment calls. - Enforce strict session token regeneration protocols upon user authentication across all internal web applications.
Customer support platform security relies on robust session lifecycle management and prompt patch execution to ensure helpdesk portals remain protected from unauthenticated session hijacking vectors. #CodeDefence #Zammad #Helpdesk #SessionFixation #PrivilegeEscalation #CISA #KEV #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: Microsoft warns of escalating OAuth consent phishing attacks abusing malicious Azure cloud application registrations
item.description:
Cloud security research writeups published today warn of widespread threat campaigns leveraging illicit consent grants to establish persistent access across enterprise cloud tenants. Threat actors trick users into granting administrative API permissions to rogue application registrations.
The attack methodology abuses OAuth 2.0 authorization workflows in Microsoft Entra ID formerly Azure Active Directory. Threat actors deploy deceptive web applications requesting high-privilege Graph API scopes like Mail.ReadWrite and Files.ReadWrite.All. When corporate users grant consent, attackers receive persistent OAuth refresh tokens, allowing them to access corporate email mailboxes, download cloud files, and exfiltrate tenant data without triggering traditional password reset alerts or multi-factor authentication prompts.
Subverting cloud identity permissions via illicit consent grants bypasses traditional perimeter access barriers. Because OAuth refresh tokens remain valid regardless of password updates, unmonitored consent grants permit threat actors to maintain persistent access to corporate cloud assets undetected.
- Enforce admin consent requirements in Microsoft Entra ID, restricting unprivileged users from consenting to multi-tenant applications. - Audit active OAuth application consent grants across cloud tenants, revoking permissions for unverified third-party applications. - Implement conditional access policies restricting OAuth token issuance based on trusted device compliance and location rules. - Deploy identity threat detection to flag anomalous Graph API data access volumes originating from third-party OAuth apps.
Cloud identity governance demands strict OAuth consent controls and continuous application auditing to ensure corporate cloud tenants remain insulated from persistent illicit consent exploitation. #CodeDefence #Microsoft #EntraID #Azure #OAuth #IdentitySecurity #CloudSecurity #Phishing #AppSec
